cables.name: LDF4-50A
cables.family: HELIAX LDF (1/2 in low-density foam, corrugated copper)
cables.rating: Black PE jacket; no NEC/UL fire listing on the sheet (EN 50575 Euroclass Fca). Outdoor/general use.
cables.use: General 1/2 in feeder and jumpers outdoors (roof donor runs); indoors only where the code allows an unlisted PE jacket (e.g. in metal raceway).
cables.vendor: CommScope HELIAX (now ANDREW, an Amphenol company)
cables.note: 1-8800 MHz; 40 kW peak; 0.815 dB/100 ft at 150 MHz. 850/1900/2600 MHz are not tabulated; nearest listed rows given instead (no interpolation). Sheet dated 2018.

cables.name: LDF4RK-50A
cables.rating: Riser: fire retardancy test method NFPA 130-2010 | UL 1666 / CATVR / CMR. Non-halogenated fire-retardant polyolefin jacket.
cables.use: In-building riser (vertical, floor-to-floor) and general runs where a CATVR/CMR cable is accepted; not for plenum air-handling spaces.
cables.note: Same attenuation table as LDF4-50A on the sheet. 1-8800 MHz.

cables.name: HL4RPV-50
cables.rating: Plenum: fire retardancy test method NFPA 262 / CATVP / CMP. Off-white PVC jacket.
cables.use: 1/2 in distribution antenna cable in plenum ceilings and anywhere a plenum cable is required.
cables.note: Air dielectric with PE spline. Installation temperature -5 C to +60 C (+23 F to +140 F) - cold-weather pulls limited. Single-bend radius not on the sheet.

cables.name: AVA5-50
cables.rating: Black PE jacket; no NEC fire listing on the sheet.
cables.use: Long 7/8 in donor/backbone runs outdoors or in raceway where loss matters more than size.
cables.note: 1-5000 MHz. Sheet revised 2018; confirm the current ANDREW revision when ordering.

cables.name: AVA5RK-50
cables.family: HELIAX Virtual Air 7/8 in, fire-retardant jacket
cables.rating: Riser: NFPA 130-2010 | UL 1666 / CATVR / CMR. Non-halogenated fire-retardant polyolefin jacket.
cables.use: 7/8 in riser backbone in buildings where CATVR is accepted (not plenum).
cables.note: Same attenuation as AVA5-50 on the sheet. 1-5000 MHz.

cables.name: AVA6-50
cables.rating: Black PE jacket; no NEC fire listing on the sheet.
cables.use: Very long trunk runs (campus, tunnel head-end, tower) where 7/8 in loss is too high.

cables.name: AVA7-50
cables.rating: Black PE jacket; no NEC fire listing on the sheet.
cables.use: Main feeders where the lowest loss is needed; heavy and stiff.
cables.note: Operating band 1-2700 MHz only - does not cover 3.x GHz.

cables.name: LDF5-50A (obsolete)
cables.rating: Black PE jacket; NEC classification N/A on the 2002 Andrew sheet.
cables.use: Legacy installs only - you will meet it in existing buildings; for new work order a current 7/8 in cable (e.g. AVA5-50 or RFS LCF78-50JA) after confirming availability.
cables.note: The CommScope sheet (2010) is marked OBSOLETE. OD differs by source: 1.030 in (CommScope 2010) vs 1.08 in (Andrew 2002); the 2002 sheet gives a 10 in minimum bend radius. Old Andrew connector part numbers on the 2002 sheet: L5PNM-RC (N male), L5PNF-RC (N female), L5PDM-RC (7-16 male), L5PDF-RC (7-16 female).

cables.name: FSJ1-50A
cables.rating: PE jacket; no NEC fire listing on the sheet.
cables.use: Short equipment jumpers and tight-bend pigtails only - high loss per foot.
cables.note: 1-18000 MHz. Sheet revised 2013.

cables.name: LCF12-50J
cables.rating: Black polyethylene jacket (UL 1581 UV resistance). No plenum/riser listing on the sheet; 'intended for outdoor usage'.
cables.use: Outdoor 1/2 in jumpers and feed transitions; GPS lines.
cables.note: Max frequency 8.8 GHz; 38 kW peak. 150 MHz not tabulated (100 MHz 0.66, 200 MHz 0.95). Recommended/max clamp spacing 0.6/1 m (2/3.25 ft).

cables.name: LCF78-50JA
cables.rating: Black polyethylene jacket; PIM min -160 dBc; no plenum/riser listing on the sheet ('intended for outdoor usage').
cables.use: 7/8 in main feed lines outdoors / in raceway.
cables.note: Max frequency 5 GHz (title says supports CBRS/C-Band to 4.2 GHz); 85 kW peak; clamp spacing 0.8/1 m. 150 MHz not tabulated.

cables.name: LCF78-50JFNA
cables.family: RFS CELLFLEX 7/8 in, flame-retardant halogen-free jacket
cables.rating: Riser: UL 1581; UL 1666; NEC type CATVR; NFPA 130 (2014) Ch.12 via UL 1685/FT4/IEEE 1202; IEC 60332-3-24, IEC 61034, IEC 60754 (LS0H).
cables.use: Indoor 7/8 in riser/backbone where CATVR is accepted.
cables.note: Installation temperature -15 C to +60 C. Its table is slightly higher than the black-PE LCF78-50JA (0.99 vs 0.95 dB/100 ft at 700 MHz) - both sheets dated 2024-01-15.

cables.name: LCF158-50JA
cables.rating: Black polyethylene jacket; PIM min -160 dBc; outdoor.
cables.use: Lowest-loss main feed lines.
cables.note: Max frequency 2.75 GHz; 310 kW peak.

cables.name: SCF12-50J

components.type: BDA / DAS battery backup unit (secondary power)
components.what: A cabinet of batteries and a charger that keeps the BDA or each DAS remote running when building AC fails, and reports AC-fail, charger-fail and low-battery alarms. Vendors list their BBUs as UL 2524 together with their own amplifiers, so the BBU is normally bought from the same maker as the BDA.
pick_by: Runtime at the actual load: hours = capacity over load (Comba gives Backup Hours = 48.1 x Ah / load W; Fiplex rates 100 W for 24 h or 200 W for 12 h); size from the BDA's stated power draw, not its nameplate
Runtime the AHJ requires (vendor sheets offer 12 h and 24 h configurations; the code requirement is checked separately) and how many units in parallel reach it
Listed combination: the BBU must appear in the BDA's UL 2524 listing (ADRF and Comba list specific BDA + BBU pairings)
Chemistry: sealed lead-acid (Fiplex, ADRF) vs LiFePO4 (Comba); weight and floor or wall loading
Voltage matching the BDA (24 V Fiplex, 12/24/48 V ADRF, 51.2 V Comba)
Enclosure rating (NEMA 4 on all sheets checked) and operating temperature (Comba BBU 0-40 C vs BDA -40-55 C)
Built-in annunciator and alarm outputs; EPO switch input
Seismic (HCAI/OSHPD OSP) variants where needed
ratings: UL 2524 listed (Fiplex 2nd Ed. via SGS; ADRF 2nd Ed. via UL with named PSR models; Comba BBU SGS cert SGSNA/23/GZ/00235X)

components.note: The ADRF sheet shows a single 48 Ah unit gives 5.8-11.4 h on its own repeaters, so several units in parallel are needed to reach a 12 h or 24 h target. Fiplex's integrated HONBDA-7S cabinet carries its own 2 lead-acid batteries for 24 h at maximum consumption (65 W, or 80 W at 2W) (source act_fiplex_bd441). ADRF's adrftech.com page describes ADRF-BBU-W as a wall-mount 12/24/48 V unit, UL 2524 Second Edition, 'up to 24-hour runtime' (source act_adrf_psru1); no spec sheet was opened for it. The Fiplex BD105 sheet's metric size line (25.4 mm for 10 in) is a typo on the sheet; the inch figures are used here.

components.what: A sealed, gasketed box rated against hose-directed water (Type 4), and also corrosion (Type 4X, usually stainless). Public-safety BDAs, DAS units and BBUs from the vendors checked already ship in their own NEMA 4 housings; a separate enclosure is for equipment that comes without a rated housing.
pick_by: Type rating actually required (4 vs 4X); 4X for corrosive or washdown spaces
Material: painted carbon steel (Type 4) vs 304 or 316/316L stainless (Type 4X)
Inside size: the back-panel size, not the outside size, must fit the equipment plus bend radius for coax and fiber
Listing on the maker's sheet (Hoffman and Hammond list these under UL 508A Types 3R/4/4X/12 and CSA C22.2 No. 94)
Door style (continuous hinge with clamps), padlock provision, bonding and grounding studs
Entry: these boxes ship without knockouts, so plan sealed Type 4X fittings for every cable entry
Heat: sealed boxes need checked heat dissipation (vendor BDA sheets list BTU/hr)
ratings: UL 508A Listed Type 3R, 4, 4X, 12 (nVent HOFFMAN, File No. E61997; Hammond)
BDA vendor housings: NEMA 4 / UL 50 (Fiplex), UL50E Type 4 / NEMA 4 (Comba), NEMA 4 (ADRF)

Seamless foam-in-place gasket, padlock hasp, bonding provision on door, grounding stud on body. components.note: Neither Hoffman nor Hammond cites UL 50/50E on these sheets; both cite UL 508A. Whether an AHJ accepts a separate enclosure around listed BDA gear is not stated on any vendor sheet; the Fiplex, Comba and ADRF BDAs and BBUs carry their own NEMA 4 / Type 4 housings as listed. Hammond's catalog says 14 gauge in the 1418 N4 SS series section but 16 gauge for its junction-box series; the series section is used here. Saginaw was not checked.

components.type: 2-hour fire-rated pathway / survivability for backbone cable (UL 2196 coax, circuit-protective wrap)
components.what: Ways to keep the riser and backbone feeding the antennas working for 2 hours in a fire: a coax that is itself listed to UL 2196 as part of a UL FHIT circuit-integrity system, or a listed wrap system around ordinary cable or raceway. A 2-hour rated shaft or room is the other route; that is building construction, not a product.
pick_by: Listed system, not just the cable: the UL FHIT system number and its required supports (strut, clamps, spacing) must be followed as listed
Hours rated (2 h) and whether the hose-stream test is included
Attenuation at the job's bands, both normal and during fire (RFS publishes both); fire-rated 1/2 in coax loses more than standard 1/2 in
Plenum or riser rating (CATVP / CMP) where the cable runs
Clamp spacing and minimum bend radius from the sheet
Connectors: whether standard connectors from the same maker are allowed
Wrap systems: number of layers per listed system, ampacity derating, weight per foot
AHJ acceptance of the specific listing (outside the scope of vendor sheets)
ratings: UL 2196 circuit integrity, 2 hour (RFS DragonSkin: UL System FHIT 1250; Radio Solutions CAFR-20A: ETL-listed to UL 2196)
NEC Article 820 CATVP to UL 1655 / NFPA 262 plenum (RFS); CMP plenum (CAFR-20A)
ASTM E1725 / UL 1724 electrical circuit protective system up to 3 hour (3M Interam E-5A-4, layered per listed system)

part_examples.spec_summary: 1/2 in air-dielectric corrugated coax, solid copper inner 4.8 mm (0.19 in), corrugated copper outer 13.8 mm (0.54 in), red plenum PVC jacket 18 mm (0.71 in). Certified to UL 2196, survives 2 hours up to 1,850 F plus water spray without conduit or wrap. UL System FHIT 1250; UL R40176, E239351; NEC 820 CATVP to UL 1655, NFPA 262; CSA C22.2 FT6. Max frequency 1 GHz; 50 ohm; VSWR 1.5 (14 dB RL) 10-1000 MHz. Loss dB/100 ft at 20 C / during fire at 1010 C: 150 MHz 0.90 / 1.80; 450 MHz 1.59 / 3.15; 700 MHz 2.07 / 4.04; 800 MHz 2.22 / 4.33 (fire figures from a 100 ft sample with 10 ft burned). 0.34 lb/ft; bend radius 7 in single / 10 in repeated; clamp spacing 2 ft; uses standard RFS connectors.

1/2 in 2-hr rated fire-resistive coax, CMP plenum, ETL certified and listed to UL 2196. Solid copper center 0.188 in, corrugated copper outer 0.550 in, max jacket 0.63 in. 50 ohm, max 1 GHz, VSWR 1.50. Attenuation dB/100 ft: 150 MHz 1.12; 450 MHz 2.32; 600 MHz 2.88; 700 MHz 3.20; 800 MHz 3.56; 900 MHz 3.86. 0.27 lb/ft, min bend radius 8 in, clamp spacing 2 ft. Listed installation requires min 12 GA x 1-5/8 x 1-5/8 in galvanized steel strut (fasteners max 9 in o.c.) and min 16 GA x 1-1/4 in galvanized steel cable clamps with #10 steel bolt. Sheet version 5.4, 8/25/2021.

Endothermic wrap for electrical circuitry, including raceways, cables, cable trays, junction boxes, conduits and distributed antenna systems (named on the sheet). Up to 3 hour electrical circuit protection per ASTM E1725 / UL 1724; 1-, 2- and 3-hour ratings set by the number of layers in the listed system. Mat 0.408 in (10.3 mm) thick; roll 24.5 in x 20 ft (40.8 sq ft), 74.6 lb; 1.83 lb/sq ft. ASTM E84 flame spread 0.7, smoke 0. Sheet cites IEEE P848 ampacity derating and says normal-condition heat from power cables can dissipate through the mat. Installed with stainless steel banding and 3M foil tape 425 per listed system details. Technical data sheet October 2019.

components.note: The listing belongs to the whole installed system (cable plus its supports), so the BOM must carry the strut, clamps and spacing named in the listing, not just the cable. The 3M sheet names UL 1724 but not a system number for DAS coax; the system number has to come from the listing directory. No UL 2196 / circuit-integrity singlemode fiber cable was found in this pass. Fire-rated wrap from Alkegen/Unifrax (FyreWrap) came up only as grease-duct and flue products, not as an electrical circuit system, so it is not listed here. A reseller page claims DragonSkin is the only standalone UL 2196 coax; CAFR-20A's sheet contradicts that.

components.type: Singlemode fiber cable for DAS (OS2; riser OFNR, plenum OFNP, armored) and connector polish (SC/APC vs LC/UPC)
components.what: The backbone between a fiber DAS master (or fiber optic unit) and its remote units. Fiplex and Comba fiber DAS both run on singlemode, one strand per remote with WDM, so the cable is OS2 tight-buffered indoor cable rated for the space it runs in, terminated with the connector polish the DAS vendor specifies.
pick_by: Fiber type: singlemode OS2 (ITU-T G.652.D; bend-insensitive G.657 where tight routing is expected)
NEC listing for the space: OFNR riser, OFNP plenum, OFCP for interlocking-armored plenum
Fiber count: one strand per remote on single-strand WDM systems, plus spares and redundant paths
Armored (interlocking aluminum) where crush protection is needed; it raises OD and bend radius
Max attenuation dB/km and the DAS optical budget (Fiplex 20 dBo max; Comba 6.5 dBo end to end)
Connector polish set by the DAS vendor: Comba V3 NG requires SC/APC or fusion splices only, no LC/UPC anywhere in the path; Fiplex FLEX 2.0 uses LC/UPC with optical return loss >45 dB
Connector return loss: Panduit OS2 UPC cords 55 dB min; APC cords 65 dB min
Bend radius and pulling tension from the sheet
ratings: NEC Article 770 OFNR (UL 1666 riser) / OFNP (NFPA 262 plenum) / OFCP (armored plenum)
ICEA S-83-596 indoor cable design and test

part_examples.spec_summary: 12-fiber OS2, ITU-T G.652.D, 900 um tight buffer; max attenuation 0.4 dB/km at 1310 / 1383 / 1550 nm. Riser (OFNR): NEC OFNR, UL 1666, CSA FT-4. OD 6.1 mm (0.24 in). Min bend radius 91.5 mm (3.6 in) installing, 61 mm (2.4 in) installed. Max tensile 660 N (148.37 lbf) short-term / 200 N (44.96 lbf) long-term for 12F. All-dielectric, no grounding or bonding.

part_examples.spec_summary: 12-fiber OS2, G.652.D, 0.4 dB/km max at 1310/1383/1550 nm. Spirally wrapped aluminum interlocking armor, up to seven times the crush protection of unarmored. Plenum (OFCP): NEC OFCP, NFPA 262, CSA FT-6. OD 11.3 mm (0.44 in) over a 6 mm inner cable; min bend radius 170 mm (6.69 in) installing, 113 mm (4.45 in) installed; 440 N short-term / 132 N long-term tensile; 113 kg/km (75.93 lb/1000 ft). Unarmored plenum twin: 012E88-33131-29 (OFNP, OD 6 mm).

part_examples.part: FISD012R9 (FX Indoor OS2 Distribution Tight Buffer, 12 fibers, OFNR, yellow)
part_examples.spec_summary: 12-fiber OS2 indoor distribution, 900 um tight buffer, core 8.2/125 um, MFD 9.2 um. Max attenuation 0.5 dB/km at 1310 nm and 1550 nm. UL Type OFNR / c(UL) OFNR, FT4 (print legend). Min bend radius 20x OD installing, 10x OD installed.

components.note: Why APC on RF-over-fiber, as stated by vendor sheets: Comba's V3 NG fiber DAS sets an end-to-end reflectance limit of -60 dB and requires SC/APC connectors or fusion splices with no LC/UPC anywhere between the fiber optic unit and the remotes. Panduit rates its APC cords at 65 dB min return loss vs 55 dB min for OS2 UPC cords. Fiplex FLEX 2.0 instead ships LC/UPC ports with >45 dB optical return loss. So the jumper BOM depends on the DAS brand: Comba's sheet forbids UPC in its fiber path; Fiplex's sheet does not address APC. An APC connector does not mate with a UPC connector, so every jumper and panel adapter in one path must share one polish. General background (not from a cited sheet): analog RF links are sensitive to light reflected back into the laser, which is why APC's angled end face is preferred. Corning's 012E88-33131-29 sheet lists a weight of 3.38 kg/km that looks wrong for a 6 mm cable, so weight is left out for that part. CommScope and AFL cable sheets were not opened.

components.type: Fiber jumpers, pigtails and patch panels (fiber distribution)
components.what: Patch cords connect the DAS master, fiber optic unit and remotes to the building fiber; adapter panels and pigtailed panels in a wall or rack housing terminate the backbone cable. Polish (APC or UPC) and connector (SC or LC) must match the DAS equipment ports end to end.
pick_by: Connector and polish at each end, matched to the DAS port (Comba FOU: SC/APC; Fiplex FLEX 2.0: LC/UPC); hybrid cords where port and panel differ in connector type, never in polish
Fiber type OS2, jacket rating (OFNR riser or LSZH), cord OD (1.6 mm vs 3.0 mm) and length
Connector insertion loss and return loss against the DAS optical budget
Panel adapter count, simplex vs duplex, adapter color (green = APC on Corning CCH)
Pigtailed panel when the backbone is fusion-spliced inside the housing
Housing for the panels (wall-mount or rack) sized for fiber count and spares
ratings: OFNR riser or LSZH cord jackets (Panduit)
TIA-604-3 (FOCIS-3, SC) and TIA-604-10 (FOCIS-10, LC); TIA-568.3 (Panduit APC sheet)

part_examples.spec_summary: Singlemode OS2/A2; 1.6 mm cord G.657.A2/B2, 3.0 mm cord G.652.D. LC/APC or SC/APC, simplex or duplex, riser (OFNR) or LSZH, yellow. Insertion loss 0.30 dB max LC/APC, 0.50 dB max SC/APC; return loss 65 dB min. Min bend radius 16 mm (1.6 mm cord), 29 mm (3 mm cord). Durability 500 cycles. Sheet example F92ERB1B1SNM5.5 = OS2, 2-fiber, 1.6 mm, riser, LC/APC to LC/APC, standard IL, 5.5 m. Connector codes include ANAN (SC/APC-SC/APC), ANB1 (SC/APC-LC/APC), ANNN (SC/APC pigtail).

part_examples.spec_summary: OS2 LC or SC (UPC), simplex or duplex, riser (OFNR) or LSZH. Insertion loss standard 0.25 dB max (LC OS2), 0.50 dB max (SC OS2); return loss 55 dB min (OS2). Fiber code 9 = OS2. LC/APC and SC/APC options are listed as 'contact Panduit for part number' on this sheet. Hybrid cords put the SC on End B.

part_examples.spec_summary: Closet Connector Housing adapter panel, 12 SC simplex adapters, APC, ceramic inserts, green composite housing, for factory or field connectors in LANscape housings. Pigtailed version CCH-CP12-6C-P03RH carries factory-terminated SC/APC simplex pigtails, 3 m (9.84 ft), for splicing the backbone inside the housing.

components.note: Panduit's UPC sheet does not print a full OS2 part number; the pattern is from its ordering key, so confirm the exact number with Panduit before ordering. The CCH panels need a Corning CCH housing (wall or rack); no housing sheet was opened. Corning UPC equivalents named by a reseller (CCH-CP12-3C simplex, CCH-CP12-59 duplex) were not verified on Corning sheets.

components.what: A dedicated panel, usually at the fire command center, that shows the radio system's status with LEDs and a buzzer, plus dry-contact outputs that the fire alarm control unit monitors. Vendors build it to their own BDA and BBU and include it in their UL 2524 listing.
pick_by: Which alarms it shows (sheets list: AC normal, loss of AC, charger failure, low battery capacity, donor antenna disconnect, donor antenna malfunction, active RF emitter malfunction, system component malfunction)
Compatibility: built for the same vendor's BDA/BBU and listed with it
Dry-contact outputs to the FACP (number of Form C relays, one per alarm) and how many monitor modules that takes at the FACP
Wiring: conductor count, protocol (RS-485 on Comba) and max cable distance to the panel location
Power source (from BBU/BDA DC) and draw
Mounting (wall box size, flush vs surface) and enclosure rating
Number of remote annunciators supported per BBU or BDA
ratings: UL 2524 listed or certified with the vendor's system (Comba SGS cert SGSNA/21/GZ/00021; Fiplex BBU with built-in annunciator UL2524 2nd Ed. via SGS)

part_examples.spec_summary: External annunciator for Comba V1/V2 BBUs and V3 BDA/fiber BDA. Visual and audible annunciation of UL 2524 alarms: AC input normal, loss of normal AC power, battery charger failure, loss of battery capacity, active RF emitting device malfunction, system component malfunction, donor antenna disconnection, donor antenna malfunction; panel also shows panel comm fault and panel normal power. Optional dry-contact alarm outputs to the FACP. UL50E Type 4; 11.8 x 7.9 x 4.4 in, 11 lb; +12 to +60 VDC, 3 W, powered from the BBU; RS-485, 5 conductors (3 RS-485 + 2 DC), max 2,000 ft on 24 ga or 4,000 ft on 18 ga; 8 knockouts; wall mount. UL2524 2nd Edition via SGS, cert SGSNA/21/GZ/00021. Sheet DS-Control 0-0-8 / 0224.

part_examples.part: HONBDA-BTTY-100100 (BBU with built-in annunciator; port for external annunciators)
part_examples.spec_summary: Annunciator built into the 100 Ah / 24 VDC BBU, showing AC power normal, AC power failure, battery capacity <30%, battery charger fail, donor antenna disconnection, donor antenna malfunction, RF emitter fail, system component fail. Up to 4 flush wall-mounted annunciators may connect to one BBU. NEMA-4 BBU enclosure; UL2524 2nd Edition listed with SGS. The HONBDA-7S all-in-one cabinet also carries an LED + dry-contact annunciator. No separate remote annunciator part number appears on these sheets.

part_examples.spec_summary: Dedicated supervised annunciator showing AC power, antenna, charger and low battery status; mounts in a standard electrical 2-gang box. BDA provides two Form C relays for each trouble: AC power status, charger status, low battery capacity, BDA trouble, antenna trouble, aux alarm; second relay set feeds the LED annunciator panel. Donor antenna line monitored. System listings UL2524 S36081, CSFM 7300-0028:0508. Sheet DN-61014:C dated 12/11/18 (older generation).

part_examples.part: Annunciator supplied with PSR-78-9537-U (part number not printed on that sheet; adrftech.com names PSR-ANN-L for its fiber remotes)
part_examples.spec_summary: Part of the UL 2524 Second Edition listed solution (repeater + annunciator + ADRF-BBx-U battery). Annunciator 5.91 x 2.84 x 6.32 in (without bracket), 2.5 lb, 100 dB at 1 m. Repeater dry-contact alarms: loss of normal AC power, battery charger failure, low battery capacity, donor antenna malfunction/disconnection, active RF emitting device malfunction, system component malfunction.

components.note: Each vendor's annunciator is listed with its own BDA/BBU; none of the sheets claims cross-vendor use. Avire's SAFE-AN-1002 remote annunciator guide was opened but has no electrical or alarm-list specs, so it is not used.

components.type: Donor-line supervision, EPO and alarm-interface accessories
components.what: Small vendor accessories around the BDA: a donor-antenna line sensor or end-of-line termination so the BDA can report a cut or failed donor line, a coax surge protector on the roof feed, and an emergency power-off (EPO) switch wired to the BDA or BBU. Most current BDAs build the monitoring in and only need these add-ons.
pick_by: Whether the BDA monitors the donor line itself (Fiplex, ADRF, Comba, Nextivity sheets list donor antenna disconnect/malfunction alarms) or needs the vendor's sensor/termination at the antenna end
Same-vendor accessory named in the BDA's ordering list, so it stays inside the listed system
EPO input on the BDA/BBU (Fiplex HONBDA-7S, Comba BBU, Nextivity terminal block) and the switch's power type and enclosure rating
Surge protector frequency range, connector and listing for the donor feed
Spare external alarm inputs on the BDA (Comba: 5, #5 pre-set for door open) and RF test ports for commissioning (Comba: SMA, -28 +/-4 dB coupling)
ratings: UL listed coax surge protector (Notifier BDA-LA-P8AX-6G, per sheet)

part_examples.spec_summary: Antenna sensor / end-of-line termination for the NF-BDA series; the sheet states the donor antenna line is monitored for integrity. No electrical specs printed. Sheet DN-61014:C, 12/11/18.

das.requirement: Repeaters, transmitters, receivers, signal-booster components, remote annunciators and operational consoles, power supplies and battery charging components must be listed and labeled to UL 2524.
das.detail: IFC 2024 510.4 says equipment providing in-building ERCES shall be listed in accordance with UL 2524. Passive parts (cable, splitters, couplers, antennas) are not on NFPA's UL 2524 list, but NFPA 1225 18.12.1.1 requires RF-emitting devices and cabling to be approved by the AHJ and the frequency license holder. UL describes UL 2524 as covering safety (fire, shock), performance against IFC-2018 / NFPA 1221 (2019), and marking/installation documents. Vendor sheets cite 2nd or 3rd Edition; a 3rd edition is cited by Fiplex but was not confirmed on a UL page.

das.requirement: BDA, repeater, receiver, transmitter, fiber optical-to-RF/RF-to-optical converters and external filters in NEMA 4 or 4X enclosures; batteries in NEMA 3R or better; batteries that need venting in NEMA 3R.
das.detail: IFC 2024 says 'NEMA Type 4 cabinet' for all signal booster components and NEMA 3R or higher for battery systems. The 2018 IFC wording was 'NEMA 4-type waterproof cabinet'. The BDAs and BBUs in the components list ship in their own NEMA 4 / Type 4 housings.

das.requirement: 12 hours at 100% system load: a dedicated battery, an AHJ-approved alternative, or a 2-hour battery plus a facility generator that can carry the full load for 12 hours.
das.detail: Primary power must be a dedicated branch circuit, permanently connected, NFPA 72 compliant and protected from overvoltage (18.13.1). IFC 510.6.1 annual testing loads batteries for 1 hour. Size battery cabinets from the vendor's runtime table at the real load, not the nameplate Ah.

das.topic: Supervisory signals to the fire alarm system
das.requirement: The ERCES must be monitored by a listed fire alarm control unit (or, where approved, an audible signal at a constantly attended location).
das.detail: IFC 2024 list: loss of normal AC, battery charger failure, signal source malfunction, active RF-emitting device failure, low battery at 70% of the 12-hour capacity depleted, failure of critical components, the FACU-to-ERCES communications link, and oscillation. A single supervisory input may be allowed where approved. NFPA 1225 requires NFPA 72 Chapter 10 integrity monitoring of the same list.

das.requirement: A dedicated annunciator in the fire command center with visual, labeled indications per component and RF-emitting device.
das.detail: Indications: normal AC, loss of AC, battery charger failure, low battery (70% depletion), signal source malfunction, active RF-emitting device malfunction, active system component malfunction; the link to the annunciator is supervised. The annunciator is itself on the UL 2524 list (18.12.1.3).

das.requirement: Fully sprinklered (NFPA 13) buildings: backbone cables and components need no fire-resistance rating. Non-sprinklered, partially sprinklered or high-rise buildings: use a cable with a listed fire-resistance rating or run it in a protected enclosure/area.
das.detail: Required rating follows the building's primary structural frame: 2 hours where the frame needs 2 hours or more (or heavy timber); 1 hour where it needs less than 2; none where it needs none. If cables run in a rated enclosure, the backbone-to-distribution-antenna-cable connection must be inside it and penetrations firestopped to the same rating; not required when both backbone cable and components are themselves fire rated. The committee rejected metal conduit as fire protection. Example listed cable: RFS DragonSkin 2HB12-50JPLR (UL 2196 2 h, FHIT 1250, max 1 GHz).

das.topic: Older-edition survivability rules (jurisdictions still on them)
das.requirement: NFPA 72-2013 and NFPA 1221-2016: 2-hour riser coax. NFPA 1221-2019: backbone routed through an enclosure matching the building's fire rating.
das.detail: Taken from the Safer Buildings Coalition and Honeywell comparison tables, not the standards themselves. Ask the AHJ which edition is adopted.

das.requirement: All ERCES cables installed per NEC (NFPA 70) Chapters 7 and 8; the NEC sets which listed coax type goes where.
das.detail: NEC coax types: CATVP plenum (air-handling spaces; can substitute anywhere), CATVR riser (vertical runs through floors), CATV general purpose, CATVX limited use; vertical runs through more than one floor need CATVR or CATVP unless in metal raceway (EC&M, 2007-era NEC). Datasheets map tests to types: NFPA 262/UL 910 = CATVP/CMP; UL 1666 = CATVR/CMR. The SBC table summarizes NFPA 1225 as requiring plenum-rated backbone and distribution antenna cable; the 18.12.3.1 text itself only points to NEC Chapters 7 and 8 - many AHJs require plenum everywhere, so check local amendments. The 2023 NEC moved general Chapter 8 rules into Article 800; that numbering was not checked against NFPA 70 here.

das.requirement: Mechanical protection and raceways for coax per NEC Article 820.
das.detail: Committee statement: only cables subject to physical damage need protection; not all cable must be in conduit.

das.topic: Lightning / surge protection on the donor line
das.requirement: Each donor antenna coax gets a listed antenna discharge unit per NEC Art. 820, listed to UL 497C; antenna, mast and discharge unit grounded per Art. 820.
das.detail: The 2022 edition dropped the earlier NFPA 780 reference because NFPA 780 covers the structure, not equipment. Check the arrestor's listing: several PolyPhaser sheets in the components list cite UL 497E, while NFPA 1225 names UL 497C - confirm with the vendor/AHJ before ordering.

das.topic: Grounding the coax shield at entry
das.requirement: Bond the coax outer conductor to the building grounding system as close as practicable to the point of entrance.
das.code: NEC 820.100 (older numbering, as summarized by EC&M 2007)
das.detail: Bonding conductor: insulated copper, at least 14 AWG, need not exceed 6 AWG, current capacity at least that of the outer conductor, as short and straight as practicable; terminate at the nearest accessible point of the grounding electrode system. Grounding kits (ANDREW SureGround SG12-12B2U / SG78-12B2U, RFS GKSPEED) use 6 AWG / 16 mm2 leads.

das.requirement: Donor antennas permanently affixed, or on an approved movable sled with the 'movement or repositioning prohibited' sign; isolation between donor and all inside antennas at least 20 dB above system gain.
das.detail: Antenna installation must keep the building envelope weather protection (IFC 510.5.1 / NFPA 18.3.3.3). High front-to-back donor antennas and physical separation help reach the isolation figure.

das.requirement: Signal boosters must have built-in oscillation detection and control that reduces gain and keeps operating; oscillation sends a supervisory signal; shutdown allowed only for uncorrectable oscillation.
das.detail: IFC 510.5.4 also requires a spectrum analyzer check for spurious oscillation at acceptance and every annual test.

das.topic: FCC Part 90 signal booster class, consent and registration
das.requirement: Class A: no passband over 75 kHz (channelized). Class B: a passband over 75 kHz. Non-licensees need the licensee's express consent; Class B installations are registered in the FCC signal booster database; boosters are labeled as Class A/B and 'NOT a CONSUMER device'.
das.detail: IFC 2024 also requires written authorization from the frequency license holder before first activation of certified RF-emitting devices.

das.requirement: The system must carry every frequency the AHJ requires, any modulation in current use, and be upgradeable when frequencies change.
das.detail: Pick passives whose frequency range covers every band now and planned (e.g. VHF needs 138-174 MHz-capable couplers/antennas; many low-PIM DAS passives start at 350 MHz). NFPA notes VHF changes are hard because of filters and non-standard Tx/Rx spacing.

das.requirement: Design to minimize near-far effects and include enough distribution antennas to address reduced-gain conditions.
das.detail: More, lower-power antennas reduce the chance that one nearby portable drives the uplink into gain reduction. This drives antenna count and coupler values in the BOM.

das.requirement: No code number; size cable from datasheet loss at the highest band carried, times run length.
das.detail: Example, 200 ft run at 700 MHz: LDF4-50A 1.831 dB/100 ft = 3.7 dB; AVA5-50 0.986 = 2.0 dB; LMR-400 3.4 (formula) = 6.8 dB. At 2000 MHz: LDF4-50A 3.251 = 6.5 dB vs AVA5-50 1.759 = 3.5 dB. Check every band: a run that is fine at 150 MHz can fail at 2.x GHz. Fire-resistive coax loses more in a fire (DragonSkin 700 MHz: 2.07 normal, 4.04 dB/100 ft with 10 ft burning).

das.requirement: Every passive must handle the composite average power at its position, at the highest band carried and the enclosure temperature.
das.detail: Ratings vary widely: Norsat DDC240 coupler 50 W avg; RFS CDS couplers 200 W; Microlab CK-7x1 300 W; Microlab D2-61 Wilkinson 100 W; gas-tube arrestor PolyPhaser IS-50NX-C2 375 W at 125-220 MHz but 50 W at 700-1000 MHz; Microlab TK-27 load 100 W with derating above 55 C. Unused hybrid ports must be terminated at the right power rating (Microlab CA-PS).

das.requirement: Use components with a stated PIM rating, compared at the same test level (2x20 W = 2x43 dBm is the common one).
das.detail: CommScope tests PIM with 2x20 W carriers in swept mode. Typical low-PIM ratings in this file: couplers/hybrids -160/-161 dBc (RFS, Microlab), loads -160/-161 dBc, RFS CELLFLEX -160 dBc; 4.3-10 166 dBc and NEX10 166 dBc connectors vs 160 dBc for 7-16/N (Rosenberger). Wilkinson splitters' resistors limit power and PIM (Microlab), so reactive splitters are preferred where low PIM matters. Sinclair rates its antenna at 2x3 W, so its -153 dBc is not comparable with 2x20 W ratings.

das.requirement: Check radiating cable stop bands against every band carried.
das.detail: RFS RLKU (1/2, 7/8, 1-1/4 in) list stop bands 650-750, 1330-1430 and 2025-2100 MHz and no 700 MHz row. Coupling loss is specified at 50% / 95% probability by IEC 61196-4 free-space method and RFS warns in-building results may differ.

das.requirement: Follow the DAS vendor's polish and reflectance rule.
das.detail: Comba CriticalPoint V3 NG requires SC/APC or fusion splices with no LC/UPC anywhere between the fiber optical unit and remotes, and -60 dB end-to-end reflectance; Fiplex FLEX 2.0 ships LC/UPC ports with >45 dB ORL. Order jumpers and panels to match the specific system.

das.requirement: Labeled annunciator indications; donor antenna sled sign; boosters labeled Class A/B and 'NOT a CONSUMER device'.
das.detail: No cable-labeling rule (e.g. marking ERCES coax every N feet) was found in the code text opened here; many AHJs add one in local ERCES guidelines - check them.

checklists.name: Pick a feeder cable
checklists.when: For every coax run on the floor plan, before it goes on the BOM.

items.step: Name the space the run passes through
items.detail: Air-handling plenum -> plenum (CATVP/CMP, NFPA 262) e.g. HL4RPV-50, ICA12-50JPL, HCA78-50JPL, LMR-400-LLPL. Vertical through floors -> riser (CATVR/CMR, UL 1666) or plenum, e.g. LDF4RK-50A, AVA5RK-50, LCF78-50JFNA, LMR-400-FR. Outdoor/roof -> PE-jacket hardline (LDF4-50A, AVA5-50, LCF78-50JA).

items.step: Is this run backbone in a non-sprinklered, partially sprinklered or high-rise building?
items.detail: If yes, it needs a listed fire-resistive cable (e.g. DragonSkin 2HB12-50JPLR, UL 2196 2 h) or a rated enclosure/shaft at 2 h / 1 h per the structural frame rating. DragonSkin tops out at 1 GHz.
Datasheet operating band must cover every band carried: AVA7-50 stops at 2700 MHz, LCF158-50JA 2.75 GHz, DragonSkin 1 GHz, RADIAFLEX RLKU 2700 MHz with stop bands.

items.step: Compute loss at the highest band
items.detail: Length/100 x dB/100 ft from the datasheet, plus connector and passive losses; move up a size (1/2 -> 7/8 in) if the downlink or uplink budget fails.
Compare minimum bend radius with sleeves, trays and turns (e.g. 7/8 in AVA5-50: 5 in single / 10 in multiple; LMR-400: 1 in installation / 4 in repeated).
Plenum air-dielectric and plenum LMR have narrow ranges (HL4RPV-50 install from -5 C; LMR-400-LLPL -5 to +75 C).
Prefer cable with a stated PIM figure (RFS CELLFLEX -160 dBc) or a low-PIM flexible (LMR-400-LLPX) where cellular and public safety share the DAS.
Clamp spacing from the sheet (LCF12-50J 0.6/1 m; DragonSkin 2 ft) - for fire-rated cable the listed support system is part of the listing.

checklists.name: Pick connectors
checklists.when: After the cable list is fixed, for every cable end and equipment port.

items.step: Match the connector to the exact cable
items.detail: Use the cable maker's connector for that cable (e.g. Times EZ-400-NMH-X for LMR-400; plenum TC-400-NF-PL for LMR-400-LLPL).
Read each BDA, coupler, splitter and antenna port (N, 4.3-10, 7-16, NEX10) and minimize adapters.
Multi-carrier/low-PIM paths: 4.3-10 (166 dBc) or NEX10 (166 dBc); 7-16 (160 dBc) for high-power legacy; N is common on public-safety gear but its male outer contact is easily damaged.
4.3-10 is specified to 6 GHz, 7-16 to 7 GHz (TE), N to 11 GHz, NEX10 to 20 GHz.
F and 75-ohm BNC parts do not belong in a 50-ohm DAS path.
4.3-10 screw 5 N-m (22 mm), NEX10 ~1.5 N-m (11 mm), 7-16 25-30 N-m, N per maker (0.7-1.1 N-m Rosenberger).
Add weatherproofing kits/tape for roof connections; Anritsu lists cleaning, assembly, weather wrapping and correct torque as the fixes for connector PIM.

checklists.name: Pick a splitter / coupler / hybrid
checklists.when: For each node in the distribution tree.

items.detail: Many low-PIM DAS passives start at 350 MHz (RFS CDS/TPS, Microlab CK-7x1) - for VHF use parts like Norsat DDC240 (138-960 MHz), Microlab D2-61 (70-2700 MHz) or Microlab CA-PS-2x2-196 (128-1000 MHz).
Average rating must exceed the composite power at that point (e.g. DDC240 50 W vs CK-7x1 300 W).
Take coupling from the design; note through (insertion) loss (CDS family: 1.8/0.8/0.5/0.25/0.3 dB for 6/10/15/20/30 dB).
Reactive splitters carry more power at lower PIM; Wilkinson splitters isolate outputs (>=20 dB) but resistors limit power and PIM.

items.step: PIM at a stated test level
items.detail: Compare -153 / -160 / -161 dBc only at the same tone power (2x43 dBm).
Hybrid unused outputs need a load at the right power rating (Microlab CA-PS); low-PIM loads e.g. Microlab TK-27, Radiall R404DE5050.
Same interface family as the cable plan; IP65/IP67 where needed.
Passives are not on the UL 2524 list but need AHJ and license-holder approval.

checklists.name: ERCES material compliance check
checklists.when: Before submitting the design/BOM to the AHJ and again before ordering.

items.detail: BDA/repeater, fiber master/remotes, BBU/charger, power supplies and annunciator - and confirm the listing names the exact model combination (e.g. ADRF BBU listed with named PSR models).
NEMA 4/4X for BDA, repeaters, optical converters, external filters; NEMA 3R+ for batteries.
Use the vendor runtime table at the real load (Comba: hours = 48.1 x Ah / load W; one ADRF 48 Ah BBU runs 5.8-11.4 h on its repeaters).
Wire every IFC/NFPA supervisory signal to the FACU; dedicated annunciator in the fire command center.

Sprinklered: none required. Non-/partially sprinklered or high-rise: listed fire-resistive cable or rated enclosure (2 h / 1 h per structural frame); connection inside the enclosure; firestop penetrations.
Listed antenna discharge unit (UL 497C) on each donor coax; ground antenna, mast and ADU per NEC 820; check the arrestor's UL category.
>= 20 dB above system gain; permanent mount or signed sled.
Per NEC Ch. 7-8 and any local plenum-everywhere amendment.
Class A vs B chosen with the license holder; licensee consent on file; Class B registered; written authorization before activation; boosters labeled.
Get the AHJ/license-holder frequency list and confirm every component covers it.

checklists.name: BOM review before ordering
checklists.when: Last pass before the purchase order goes out.

items.detail: Every line from a current datasheet; flag obsolete parts (the LDF5-50A sheet is stamped OBSOLETE) and renamed brands (HELIAX/ION/ERA now ANDREW, an Amphenol company).
Two ends per cable segment plus every passive and equipment port; plenum cable gets its matching connectors.
A grounding kit sized to the cable OD at each required point (SG12 fits 0.610-0.650 in jacket; SG78 1.05-1.13 in) and a ground bar.
DC pass (gas tube, e.g. Times LP-GTR) only if the line carries DC; otherwise DC-block quarter-wave/filter types; check power at the highest band.
One rated load per unused port; attenuators where the design calls for them.
Hangers/clamps at the sheet spacing; listed supports for fire-rated cable.
Polish and connector type per the DAS vendor (SC/APC vs LC/UPC); OFNR/OFNP to match the space.
Recheck runtime at the final load.
Re-add cable, connector and passive losses per branch at every band.
Order from a distributor that stocks the line (see suppliers list; check ownership changes such as Talley -> Rexel USA, Tessco private).
